findings.title: Missing AutoRealm when resolving same-thread Atomics.waitAsync promise across realms
findings.message: In js::atomics_notify_impl, when Atomics.notify() detects that the async waiter it is about to resolve was created by the *same* JSContext (waiter->cx() == cx), it takes a fast path: instead of dispatching an off-thread task to the event loop, it extracts the PromiseObject directly into a `promisesToResolve` vector and later calls PromiseObject::resolve(cx, promisesToResolve[i], resultMsg) on it after leaving the futex/helper-thread lock critical section. However, this resolve loop does not enter the promise's own realm/compartment before calling PromiseObject::resolve. A single JSContext can have multiple realms active over its lifetime (e.g. via cross-realm calls, iframes, Xrays, or realm switches performed by embedders/DevTools), so the promise created by Atomics.waitAsync() may live in a different realm than the one that happens to be current on `cx` at the time atomics_notify_impl() runs the resolve loop. Resolving/reacting to a promise while the wrong realm is entered on the context causes JS::Compartment/Realm-scoped state (i.e. currently-entered global, associated wrappers, GC arena bookkeeping tied to the compartment, and the promise reaction job queueing) to be manipulated inconsistently with the object's actual realm. This class of realm/compartment-mismatch bug in SpiderMonkey has previously led to use-after-free and type-confusion conditions because zone/compartment sweeping and off-thread promise machinery assume the context's current realm matches the object being manipulated.
findings.suggestion: Before resolving each promise in the same-thread fast path, enter the promise's own realm with AutoRealm so that PromiseObject::resolve and the subsequent promise-reaction machinery operate consistently with the object's actual realm/compartment, matching the general convention used elsewhere in SpiderMonkey when manipulating cross-realm objects.

ground_truth.root_cause: The same-thread fast path for Atomics.waitAsync()/Atomics.notify() was added without accounting for the fact that JSContext::realm() can differ from the realm of the promise being resolved; the code assumed 'same context' implied 'same realm', which is not guaranteed in a multi-realm embedding like the browser (e.g. cross-origin iframes, Xray wrappers, or other realm-switching operations happening on the same context).
